To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pharmacological inhibition of the lipid phosphatase PTEN by bispyridylvanadium compounds limits infarct size, preserves cardiac function, and attenuates apoptosis in an in vitro model of simulated ischemia-reperfussion injury and in an in vivo model of myocardial infarction.
the pharmacological inhibition PTEN by BpV(Hopic) attenuates simulated ischemia/reperfusion (SIR) in vitro and reduces myocardial infarction size and improves cardiac function in vivo.
pharmacological inhibition of phosphatase and tension homolog (PTEN) by BpV(HOpic) limits myocardial infraction size and improves cardiac function following myocardial infarction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of lipid phosphatase and tension homolog on chromosome ten (PTEN), an antagonist of phosphoinositide 4-kinase, in myocardium ischemia-reperfussion (I/R) injuries.
the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic approaches for the treatment of ischemic heart disease.
the role of PTEN and its inhibition by BpV(HOpic) in the protection of the heart from ischemia-re-perfusion injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pharmacological inhibition PTEN protects cardiomyocytes against I/R injury and limits myocardial infraction size and ameliorates cardiac dysfunction postinfarction by enhancing myocardium PI3K/AKT/eNOS/NO/ERK survival signaling pathway.
the inhibition of PTEn limits myocardial I/R injury through PI3K/AKT/eNOS/NO/ERK pathway.

the inhibition of lipid phosphatase PTEN by BpV(HPic) protects against I/R in the myocardium, and the protective effects are mediated through the upregulations of PI3K/AKT/eNOS/ERR prosurvival signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pharmacological inhibition by BpV(Hopic) of PTEN, a negative regulator of PI3K, enhances PI3K signaling and protects against I/R damage in both in vitro and in vivo models.
the pharmacological inhibition PTEN by BpV(Hopic) protects against I/R-induced cardiomyocyte death and improves cardiac function after I/R injury.
